messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bypassing beta or rc release
parts:
Daniel and I don't have the patience to sort out a beta
release and then a regular release --- it's too much fiddling
with tags, versions in R and Python, and too many changes
to the web page.

We should release Stan 2.0 in the next day or two. We're
almost there.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: bypassing beta or rc release
parts:
Ben, you're right -- we messed up the process by not having a release/v2.0.0 branch. We've already started some of the process on the develop branch when we shouldn't have.

I'll create that branch after the fixes to the manual. I'll use that branch to add the built manual and doxygen to the repository.

I'll try to be more careful next time.


Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: bypassing beta or rc release
parts:
The development branch is never supposed to be frozen under gitflow, although maybe we don't have enough manpower to always be merging pull requests. There is supposed to be a release branch from development that is not totally frozen either but only has release-related commits like bumping version numbers and stuff.

Ben
